result.question: Why can't David go into battle?

readings.answer: So that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.
readings.support: so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished

readings.answer: Because his men swore he must never again go out to battle.
readings.support: David’s men swore to him | must never again go out with us to battle

readings.answer: Because a Philistine wanted to kill him.
readings.support: the Philistine | resolved to kill David

assessments.reason: “So that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished” states the purpose of keeping David from battle, i.e., to prevent his death, matching the key’s “risk of being killed.”
“David’s men swore to him… you must never again go out… to battle” directly answers why he cannot go—because they forbid it—even though it does not restate the key’s risk-of-death rationale.

“[The Philistine] resolved to kill David” provides the immediate danger that led to the prohibition; while phrased as an assailant’s intent, it points to the same underlying risk of David being killed.

result.reason: The passage supports both the key’s reason (to avoid David’s death) and a different cause (his men’s oath forbidding him), so materially different answers fit.
